title: jnterfaces
text: jnterfaces is a package of agent skills for the command interface of a project. The interface is the Justfile, the packets that agentic Just targets emit, and the incremental file stages of cx. An agent skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file that Codex, Claude and other agents read. The documentation site is https://rahuldave.github.io/jnterfaces/. It is built from docs/. just docs previews it, and just docs-publish publishes it to the branch gh-pages. Skill Use it when just You write, change or run a Justfile, or map workflow concepts to recipes. jagt-protocol A Just target emits an AGENT_TASK v1, AGENT_RESULT v1 or AGENT_TASK_DRAFT v1 packet. cx A recipe has expensive stages that read files and write files.

title: jnterfaces
text: jnterfaces is the base of every project. Besides Git, a project needs two programs only, just and uv. One command installs everything else: just install just install comes from the file .agents/install.just, which jnterfaces installs in the project. The Justfile of the project imports that file. To start a new project, clone jnterfaces once and run its installer: git clone https://github.com/rahuldave/jnterfaces ~/.local/share/skill-packages/jnterfaces uv run ~/.local/share/skill-packages/jnterfaces/scripts/install_stack.py --profile python Start a new project gives each step, from an empty folder to a project whose checks pass. On a terminal, the installer asks which roles to install, and it saves the answers in .agents/stack.json. A named role asks nothing, and named roles alone turn on only those roles. Without a terminal, a named profile takes the default roles. A later just install installs the same set again, with no questions. So just install also updates a project.

title: jnterfaces
text: A role names a job, and a package does that job. So the package behind a role can change and the name stays. The installer asks about each role. Press Enter to keep the default: Role What it installs Package Default cx the cx skill jnterfaces no jagt-protocol the jagt-protocol skill jnterfaces no tasker the Gest g* skills, which track work agent_gest_git_skills yes prose the writing guide and its checker nossaifd yes reporter the lanes skill, which reports requests for human attention sklanes no The old names gest, nossaifd and sklanes still work. Variants. A role can have variants, such as just install tasker=gitwt. The record saves the variant, so a later just install keeps it: Variant of tasker How the work goes git, the default on a branch in the main checkout gitwt each task in its own Git worktree, and the main checkout stays on main jj with jj; not ready yet, so the installer refuses it The g* skills and the hooks of agent_gest_git_skills read the variant with just tasker-mode. In a project that jnterfaces started, the role also adds the worktree recipes just worktree-new NAME, just worktree-sync, just worktrees and just worktrees-prune. The recipes of a role. A role package can ship a recipe file, .agents/just/roles/ .just. In a project that jnterfaces started, the index imports it. For example, prose gives just prose, which checks the Markdown of the project. Another project gets the line to add to its Justfile. Starter files. A role can write a starter file, such as the AGENTS.md of tasker, once, when the project has none. The starter is yours from then on. just uninstall takes out only the lines that the role added to it, and the file stays.

title: jnterfaces
text: Install git, just and uv. Choose the folder of the package clones. The default is ~/.local/share/skill-packages. To use another folder, export SKILL_PACKAGES_DIR in your shell profile first, for example export SKILL_PACKAGES_DIR=~/Projects. just install in a project finds the clones in that folder only. Without the variable, it uses the default folder, also when you ran the first install from another clone. Clone jnterfaces into that folder: git clone https://github.com/rahuldave/jnterfaces "${SKILL_PACKAGES_DIR:-$HOME/.local/share/skill-packages}/jnterfaces" Make the project, and run the installer from the clone: mkdir app && cd app && git init uv run "${SKILL_PACKAGES_DIR:-$HOME/.local/share/skill-packages}/jnterfaces/scripts/install_stack.py" --profile python Use --profile typescript for TypeScript. The installer clones the other packages that it needs, writes the starter Justfile, and adds the tools. Run just verify. A project with no code yet passes. Put the code in the place that the profile expects: Profile Code Tests python Modules at the top of the project, such as app.py, or a package folder tests/test_NAME.py. pytest finds the modules at the top, because the test tool sets pythonpath. typescript src/, for example src/app.ts src/NAME.test.ts, which imports the code as ./app.js. Turn on the tool with just install test. Run just fmt to format the code, then just verify again. Commit the project, with .agents/, .claude/, .codex/, AGENTS.md, the Justfile and the config files. .gitignore already leaves out what a command makes again, such as .venv/ or node_modules/. Later, just install --update gets the new commits of each package, and just install --check compares the record with the files. Start a Python or TypeScript project gives each tool, recipe, hook and config file of a new project, with examples.

title: jnterfaces
text: A tool is one unit of the setup of the project, such as lint. It brings its packages, its config files and its recipes. A profile, such as python, is a language. It sets the default roles and the tools. Each profile is a package of its own, and stack.json names it: Profile Package Tools Default tools The command that adds a tool python jnprofile-python lint, test, typecheck lint, test uv add --group ... typescript jnprofile-typescript lint, test, typecheck lint, typecheck npm, which uvx runs from nodejs-wheel On the first install, the installer finds the profile from the files of the project, such as pyproject.toml, or you name it with --profile. After that, the saved record keeps the profiles, also when it has none. The recipes follow the tools. The profile package has one recipe file for each tool. just install writes a module for each profile in .agents/just, which imports the recipe files of the installed tools only. It also writes .agents/just/index.just, which .agents/install.just imports. In a project that jnterfaces started, with its starter Justfile: just python lint runs the lint of one language. just lint runs the lint of each language of the project. just verify runs every installed check of each language, then git diff --check. The starter Justfile has set allow-duplicate-recipes. So a recipe of the same name in the Justfile, such as lint, takes the place of the combined one. A project with a Justfile of its own gets the modules only, such as just python lint. .agents/stack.json records the hash of each file that just install writes in .agents/just, and the installer changes only a file whose hash is the recorded one. With more than one language, a combined recipe gives the same arguments to each language. The other files. A profile, a tool or a role adds a part to each shared file that it needs, and takes out only its part. A part is one of three kinds: a block of lines, as in .gitignore; an include that reads an own file, as the extend of ruff.toml; units, such as the items of .pre-commit-config.yaml. scripts/formats.json lists the shared files and the format of each. A package names its parts with the key parts. A profile and its tools have it in profile.json, and a role has it in install_extras.parts of skill-package.json. A role names a starter file, written once, with install_extras.starter. The key parts in .agents/stack.json records each part. just uninstall reads it to take the parts out again. The “Shared files and the record” section of docs/stack-guide.md tells how. If the project has no Justfile, the installer writes a starter Justfile. Otherwise it names the line to add to your Justfile. If the project has no pyproject.toml or package.json, the installer makes one with uv init --bare or npm init --yes. For Python, the profile also adds default-groups = "all" to pyproject.toml as a part, so that uv run has the tools. If a tool fails, a later just install tries it again. When the last package of a dependency group goes, the installer takes out the empty group.

title: jnterfaces
text: just install lint tasker turns on a tool and a role. just install tasker=gitwt turns on a role with a variant. just uninstall python takes out a profile with its tools, its recipes and its package. The project keeps pyproject.toml. just uninstall reporter lint turns them off. It removes the files of the role and the packages that just install added for the tool. It keeps each file that you edited, and each package that the project had before. You may remove a package by hand and add it back with no install between. Then it still counts as added. To keep it, take it out of owned_packages in .agents/stack.json. --profile python,typescript sets the profiles. A saved profile that the list leaves out is turned off. --defaults takes the defaults, and --all takes every role. --ask asks again, even when the project has saved choices. --update runs git pull --ff-only in each clone first. --clone NAME=DIR uses one clone in another folder. --clean installs the last commit of each clone, without uncommitted changes. --dry-run checks everything and writes nothing in the project. --check compares the record in .agents/stack.json with the shared files, and changes nothing.

title: jnterfaces
text: Each package is a Git clone in one folder. The default folder is ~/.local/share/skill-packages. Set SKILL_PACKAGES_DIR to use another folder, for example the folder of your own clones. If a clone is missing, the installer clones it from GitHub. JNTERFACES_DIR names one jnterfaces clone. Only jnterfaces has an installer. The other packages list their skills, and their other files, in skill-package.json. The installer copies them from the clone, and it writes one record for each package, such as .agents/nossaifd-install.json. A record holds the source revision and a hash of each file. The installer never overwrites or removes a file that you edited. It names the file and installs the rest. For each installed skill, it also makes the link .claude/skills/NAME for Claude Code. First it checks every package. If one check fails, it writes nothing. A record from an older installer lists no skills and no hooks. The installer then reads the files of the old source revision in the clone. So it removes the old copies of skills and hooks that it shipped, and it keeps your edits. skill-package.json names the other files of a package in install_extras: files are files or folders outside .agents/skills, such as hook scripts. The installer manages them like the files of a skill. merge_hooks are JSON settings files. The installer adds their hooks entries to the file of the same name in the project, and it takes them out again on removal. seed maps a file of the project to a starter file. The installer writes it only when the project does not have it. The list of packages, roles, aliases and profiles is in stack.json. The stack guide builds a project in layers, from a project with no code to a project with lint and tests. It says what works now and what does not. The files of the stack gives each file that the installer reads or writes, each of its keys, and how the files work together.

title: jnterfaces
text: .agents/install.just defines the variable jn_copier, which runs copier 9 through uvx. copier makes files from a template, and copier update brings in a later version of the template. Any recipe of the project can use it, for example {{jn_copier}} copy TEMPLATE FOLDER.

title: jnterfaces
text: You can also install the skills with npx: npx skills add rahuldave/jnterfaces -a codex --skill just -y The npx route installs no tools and records no source revision in .agents/. The skills use these executables: just runs the recipes, and uv runs the installer and the tools. jagt renders and checks packets, from https://github.com/rahuldave/jagt. The draft commands need a build that has jagt draft lint. cx runs incremental stages, from https://github.com/rahuldave/cx.

title: jnterfaces
text: Each package works alone, and each skill works without the optional skills: just is the only required skill. cx and jagt-protocol are optional. Each fact has one source. The packet rules are in jagt-protocol, and the cx rules are in cx. The just skill points to them. A link to a skill that may be missing has a fallback in the same paragraph, for example “If the cx skill is not installed, …”. scripts/check_skill_links.py checks this rule, and just lint runs it. The other packages run it in their CI too.

title: jnterfaces
text: Command What it does just lint Checks the syntax of the scripts, the Python and the JSON, and the links between skills. just test Runs the tests of the installers, the link checker and the skills. just install-into   [names] Runs the installer on another project. just check Runs just lint and just test. Every commit must pass it. just package-lint Checks skill-package.json with skill-package-maker. just prose   Checks the Markdown with the nossaifd writing checker. The test of the jagt demo runs only with a jagt that has jagt draft lint. If the jagt on your PATH is older, set JAGT_BIN to a newer binary. The skill jagt-protocol came from the jagt repository, and the just and cx references came from agent_gest_git_skills. This repository is now the source of all three, and of the one installer.

title: Start a Python or TypeScript project
text: This page sets up a new project with every part that the stack gives. The parts are the agent skills, the task tracker, the writing checker, format, lint, tests, coverage, types, a Git hook and one full check. Each step and each example was run on 2026-10-31 in an empty folder. How the stack fits together tells how an install works. The files of the stack tells what each file holds.

title: Start a Python or TypeScript project
text: Term Meaning recipe A command in a Justfile. just NAME runs the recipe NAME. role A job of the agent skills, for example tasker. One package does the job. profile A language setup: python or typescript. tool One part of a profile, such as lint. It adds packages, config files and recipes. clone The local Git clone of a package. The installer copies the skills from it. the record .agents/stack.json in the project. It saves the profiles, roles and tools.

title: Start a Python or TypeScript project
text: Program For How to get it git Each project and each package clone The system package manager just Every recipe https://just.systems uv The installer, Python, and Node for TypeScript https://docs.astral.sh/uv gest The skills of the tasker role Install it on its own. It does not come through uv. The installer warns when it is missing. TypeScript needs no Node on the machine. uv runs node and npm from the nodejs-wheel package, version 24.

title: Start a Python or TypeScript project
text: The installer reads each package from a clone in one folder. The default folder is ~/.local/share/skill-packages. To use another folder, export SKILL_PACKAGES_DIR in your shell profile, for example: export SKILL_PACKAGES_DIR=~/Projects Set it before the first install. just install in a project finds the clones in that folder only. git clone https://github.com/rahuldave/jnterfaces "${SKILL_PACKAGES_DIR:-$HOME/.local/share/skill-packages}/jnterfaces" The installer clones each other package that it needs into the same folder.

title: Start a Python or TypeScript project
section: Step 2: make the project and install
text: mkdir app && cd app && git init uv run "${SKILL_PACKAGES_DIR:-$HOME/.local/share/skill-packages}/jnterfaces/scripts/install_stack.py" --profile python Use --profile typescript for TypeScript, or --profile python,typescript for both. At a terminal, the installer asks about each role. Add --defaults to take the defaults with no questions: Role Default What it gives tasker yes The g* skills, which track work with Gest, the agent hooks, a starter AGENTS.md and the worktree recipes prose yes The nossaifd writing guide, its checker, and just prose cx no The cx skill: run the file stages of a recipe only when they are out of date. It needs the cx program. jagt-protocol no The jagt-protocol skill: the packets of agentic recipes. It needs the jagt program. reporter no The sklanes skill: report requests for human attention to a Lanes inbox The just skill of jnterfaces is always installed. Name a role to add it later, for example just install cx. The installer then: makes pyproject.toml with uv init --bare, or package.json with npm init --yes, when the project has none; adds the default tools of the profile, with uv add --group or npm install --save-dev; writes the starter Justfile and the starter AGENTS.md. Both are yours from then on; saves the choices in .agents/stack.json. Run just alone to list the recipes. Run just verify. A project with no code yet passes.

title: Start a Python or TypeScript project
Start a Python or TypeScript project
text: Tool Default Packages Files Recipes lint yes ruff, pre-commit, in the group lint ruff.toml, .pre-commit-config.yaml fmt, lint, hook test yes pytest, pytest-cov, in the group test [tool.pytest.ini_options] in pyproject.toml test, cov typecheck no ty, in the group lint ty.toml typecheck Add the type check: just install typecheck pyproject.toml gets default-groups = "all" under [tool.uv], so that uv run has every tool. The project uses the Python that uv picks; uv init writes it as requires-python.

title: Start a Python or TypeScript project
text: Recipe What it runs Notes just setup uv sync Installs Python and each package into .venv. Run it in a new clone. just fmt ruff format Changes the files. just fmt --check only checks. just lint ruff check just lint --fix fixes what it can. just hook pre-commit install Run it once in each clone. just test pytest Extra words go to pytest: just test tests/test_app.py. With no tests yet, it passes. A selection that runs no test fails. just cov pytest --cov --cov-report=term-missing Shows the lines that no test ran. just typecheck ty check just verify fmt --check, lint, test, typecheck, then git diff --check Runs the checks of the installed tools only. It stops at the first failure. Each recipe also has a form for one language, such as just python lint. That form matters in a project with two profiles.

title: Start a Python or TypeScript project
text: Put modules at the top of the project, such as app.py, or put a package folder there. Put the tests in tests/, in files named test_NAME.py: # app.py def add(a: int, b: int) -> int: return a + b # tests/test_app.py from app import add def test_add(): assert add(1, 2) == 3 pytest finds app because the test tool adds "." to pythonpath. Then: just fmt just verify just cov

title: Start a Python or TypeScript project
text: just hook writes .git/hooks/pre-commit. Before each commit, it runs the checks of .pre-commit-config.yaml on the staged files: trailing whitespace and the end of each file; the syntax of YAML and JSON files; files larger than 1000 KB; merge conflict markers and private keys; ruff check and ruff format. A check that changes a file stops the commit. Add the change and commit again. uv run pre-commit run --all-files runs the checks on every file.

title: Start a Python or TypeScript project
text: ruff. ruff.toml reads the settings of the profile with extend. Add your settings below that line. They win. ty. Add your settings to ty.toml. pytest. Add your settings under [tool.pytest.ini_options] in pyproject.toml, beside pythonpath. If the project already has a pytest config, such as pytest.ini or [tool.pytest], the test tool does not add pythonpath. Add pythonpath = ["."] to that config yourself.

title: Start a Python or TypeScript project
Start a Python or TypeScript project
text: Tool Default Packages Files Recipes lint yes @biomejs/biome@2 biome.json fmt, lint typecheck yes typescript@7, @types/node@24 tsconfig.json typecheck test no typescript@7, @types/node@24 tsconfig.json build, test Add the tests: just install test The packages go into devDependencies of package.json. The npm cache is in .local/npm-cache, which Git ignores.

title: Start a Python or TypeScript project
text: Recipe What it runs Notes just setup npm install Installs each package of package.json into node_modules. It can update package-lock.json. Run it in a new clone. just fmt biome format --write Changes the files. just lint biome check Checks the lint rules, the format and the order of imports. just lint --write fixes what it can. just typecheck tsc --noEmit With no .ts file in src yet, it passes. just build tsc Compiles src into dist, with source maps. just test tsc, then node --test 'dist/**/*.test.js' Extra words go to node --test. With no .ts file in src yet, it passes. just verify lint, typecheck, test, then git diff --check Runs the checks of the installed tools only.

title: Start a Python or TypeScript project
text: Put the code and the tests in src/. Name each test file NAME.test.ts. tsconfig.json compiles all of src, so the build writes the tests to dist too. Import the code with the .js name that the build writes: // src/app.ts export function add(a: number, b: number): number { return a + b; } // src/app.test.ts import assert from "node:assert/strict"; import { test } from "node:test"; import { add } from "./app.js"; test("add", () => { assert.equal(add(1, 2), 3); }); The tests use node:test and node:assert, which come with Node. Then: just fmt just verify

title: Start a Python or TypeScript project
text: biome.json and tsconfig.json read the settings of the profile with extends. Add your keys beside extends. They win. For example, the profile sets a line width of 120 for Biome.

title: Start a Python or TypeScript project
text: The tasker role works on a branch in the main checkout. To work on each task in its own Git worktree, and keep the main checkout on main: just install tasker=gitwt just tasker-mode These recipes manage the worktrees: Recipe What it does just worktree-new NAME [BASE] Makes branch NAME in ../ .worktrees/NAME, sets it up, and runs just setup there just worktree-sync Sets up a worktree that another tool made just worktrees Lists the worktrees: clean or dirty, merged or not just worktrees-prune Removes the clean, merged worktrees that were idle for 2 hours Fill in the   fields of AGENTS.md. They name the project, the source folder, the docs and the branches.

title: Start a Python or TypeScript project
text: just prose checks each Markdown file that Git tracks against the writing guide. It leaves out AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and the folders of the installer. Name pages to check only them, and add -v to see the soft notes: just prose -v README.md

title: Start a Python or TypeScript project
text: Commit these files: .agents/, .claude/ and .codex/, which hold the skills, the records and the hooks; AGENTS.md and the Justfile; pyproject.toml and uv.lock, or package.json and package-lock.json; the config files: ruff.toml, .pre-commit-config.yaml, ty.toml, biome.json, tsconfig.json; .gitignore and .worktreedisposable. .gitignore already leaves out what a command makes again, such as .venv/, node_modules/, dist/, the caches and the logs of the installer. A person who clones the project runs: just setup just hook just hook is for Python only.

title: Start a Python or TypeScript project
text: Command What it does just install Installs again what the record saves just install --update Gets the new commits of each package clone first just install --check Compares the record with the files, and changes nothing just install --dry-run Checks everything, and writes nothing just uninstall typecheck Takes out a tool: its packages, its files and its recipes just uninstall reporter Takes out a role The installer never overwrites or removes a file that you edited. It names the file and installs the rest.

title: Start a Python or TypeScript project
section: What the stack does not give
text: Add these parts yourself: CI. No profile writes a GitHub Actions workflow. A workflow can run just setup and just verify. A locked setup. just setup runs uv sync, not uv sync --locked. testpaths. pytest searches the whole project for tests. Set testpaths = ["tests"] under [tool.pytest.ini_options] to search one folder. A Git hook for TypeScript. Run just verify before each commit. Coverage for TypeScript. There is no just cov. Async tests, a server, and Docker. No tool adds pytest-asyncio, a just serve recipe or a Dockerfile. A biome.jsonc with comments. The installer leaves a file with comments alone, and it names the extends entry to add. Add it yourself.

title: The files of the stack
text: This page tells you each file that the stack reads or writes, what each key in it means, and how the files work together. How the stack fits together tells you what an install does. This page tells you the files behind it. The examples come from an install into an empty Python project on 2026-10-31, with the command just install --profile python --defaults.

title: The files of the stack
text: Term Meaning package A Git repository that ships skills, for example nossaifd. clone The local Git clone of a package. The installer reads each package from its clone. role The name of a job, for example tasker. One package does the job. profile A language setup, for example python. A profile package, such as jnprofile-python, ships it. tool One unit of a profile, for example lint. It brings packages, recipes and parts. owner A thing that adds to the files of a project: jnterfaces, a profile, a tool, or a role. A tool has the key profile:tool, for example python:lint. shared file A file that more than one owner, and you, can add to, for example .gitignore or pyproject.toml. part What one owner adds to one shared file. unit The smallest piece of a part: one line, one key, one list item or one hook. record A JSON file in .agents/ that says what the installer wrote. own file A file that the installer writes whole under .agents/, for example .agents/config/python/ruff.toml or .agents/instructions/tasker.md. A shared file includes it or points to it.

title: The files of the stack
text: A project has one record of the stack, .agents/stack.json. A profile or a role does not bring a record of its own. Each run of the installer reads what the packages declare, and writes all of it into this one file. Two other names can confuse you: stack.json at the top of jnterfaces is the catalog. It lists the packages, roles and profiles. It is not in your project. .agents/ -install.json is one file for each package. It keeps the hashes of the skill files that the package copied in. It does not hold the shared files.

title: The files of the stack
text: The packages declare. The installer reads the declarations, then writes the project and its records. File Where Who writes it What it holds stack.json jnterfaces the author of jnterfaces The catalog: each package, role and profile. scripts/formats.json jnterfaces the author of jnterfaces The format of each shared file that a part can go to. skill-package.json each package the author of the package The skills and the extras of the package. profile.json each profile package the author of the profile The tools of the profile, and the parts of each tool. .agents/stack.json the project the installer The record of the stack: your choices and each part. .agents/ -install.json the project the installer The record of one package: its revision and the hash of each of its files. .agents/stack-pending.json the project the installer The state of a run that has not finished. It is gone after a run that works. .agents/stack-log.jsonl the project the installer A history of the runs. Nothing reads it to decide what to do. .agents/just/index.just and .agents/just/ .just the project the installer The modules that import the recipes of the installed tools. generated in the record keeps their hashes. .agents/just/ /*.just and .agents/just/roles/ .just the project the packages, through install_extras.files The recipe files of each tool and role. The package record keeps their hashes. .agents/config/ /... the project the installer The own files of the tools. .agents/instructions/ .md the project the installer The own file of a role. A line in AGENTS.md points to it. .agents/install.just the project the installer The recipes just install and just uninstall. .agents/skills/ and .claude/skills/ the project the installer The skills, and a link to each one for Claude Code. .claude/hooks/ and .codex/hooks/ the project the tasker role, through install_extras.files The hook scripts. The hook entries go in .claude/settings.json and .codex/hooks.json as parts. Justfile the project the installer once, then you The starter Justfile, when the project has none. It is yours from then on. .gitignore, .worktreedisposable, AGENTS.md the project the installer and you Line files. Each owner adds a block of lines.

title: The files of the stack
section: How one run uses the files
text: just install runs scripts/install_stack.py from the jnterfaces clone. The installer reads the catalog stack.json. It finds each role, profile and alias there. It reads .agents/stack.json of the project for your saved choices. Names on the command line change them. For each package that the run needs, it reads skill-package.json from the clone. For each profile, it also reads profile.json. It makes one owner from each profile, tool and role, with its lines, parts and units. scripts/formats.json tells it how to read and write each shared file. It does a dry pass over the shared files. A conflict of two owners stops the run here, before anything changes. It copies the skills and the extra files of each package. It writes .agents/ -install.json for each one. It saves your choices in .agents/stack.json, and writes the modules in .agents/just. It does this again each time that it saves the record. If the project has no Justfile, it writes the starter Justfile. If a tool needs the manifest and the project has none, it runs init of the profile. It runs the package commands of the tools, such as uv add --group lint ruff. It saves .agents/stack-pending.json, then it writes the shared files and the own files, and adds an entry to .agents/stack-log.jsonl. It saves the new parts in .agents/stack.json, and deletes .agents/stack-pending.json. A removal, such as just uninstall lint, runs the same steps. The owner is not active, so its parts go. The installer reads what to take out from the record, never from the files.

title: The files of the stack
text: The catalog has four keys: Key What it holds version The version of the format. It is 2 now. packages A list with one entry for each package. jnterfaces is first. aliases Other names for a role, for example "gest": "tasker". profiles One entry for each profile, keyed by its name. An entry of packages has these keys: Key What it means name The name of the package and of its clone folder. repository The URL to clone when the clone is missing. about One line for the questions and the help. choice The role that the package does, for example tasker. jnterfaces has none, because it is always installed. default true when a new project turns the role on, unless the profile says otherwise. needs The packages that the role needs. record The path of the package record, when it is not .agents/ -install.json. variants and default_variant The forms of a role, for example git or gitwt for tasker. A variant with "ready": false cannot be chosen yet. required_skills and optional_skills For jnterfaces only: the just skill is always installed. cx and jagt-protocol are roles of their own. An entry of profiles has package, repository, about, and detect. detect lists the files that turn the profile on in a project with no saved profile, for example pyproject.toml or uv.lock.

title: The files of the stack
text: Each package has one skill-package.json. The installer reads these keys: Key What it means repository The owner, name and URL of the package. skills Each skill, with its name and its folder. install_extras.files Files and folders outside .agents/skills that the installer copies and records like a skill, for example .agents/just/roles/nossaifd.just. install_extras.parts The parts of a role: {shared file: source file}. For example, tasker adds a line to AGENTS.md and hooks to .claude/settings.json. install_extras.starter A file that the role writes once, when the project has none, for example the first AGENTS.md. It is yours from then on. install_extras.merge_hooks and install_extras.seed The same hooks and starter for an installer from before the parts. A newer installer leaves these files to the parts. executables The programs that the package needs, with a command that checks each one.

title: The files of the stack
text: A profile package also has profile.json. Its top keys are these: Key What it means version The version of the format. It is 1 now. name, about, detect As in the catalog. manifest The file that lists the dependencies: pyproject.toml or package.json. init The manifest file and the command that makes it when it is missing: {"file": "pyproject.toml", "command": ["uv", "init", "--bare", "--no-workspace"]}. add and remove The commands that add or remove the packages of a tool. {group} takes the group of the tool. choices The default roles of the profile, for example tasker and prose. uv_default_groups For Python: the value of tool.uv.default-groups in pyproject.toml. base What the profile adds with no tool: its recipe file, and its lines, parts and files, as for a tool. tools Each tool, keyed by its name. default_tools The tools that a new project gets, for example lint and test. A tool has these keys: Key What it means packages The packages that the tool adds, for example ruff and pre-commit. group For Python: the dependency group of the packages. recipes The recipe file of the tool, for example lint.just. verify The recipes that just verify runs for the tool. lines Lines for line files: {".gitignore": [".ruff_cache/"]}. parts Parts for unit files: {"ruff.toml": "files/ruff.toml"}. files Whole files, for an installer from before the parts. A file that is also in parts goes as a part. skip_if A guard [file, text], or a list of guards. A new part is left out when any guard applies: the file has the text, for example no ruff.toml part when pyproject.toml has [tool.ruff. An empty text means that the file is there. In a TOML file, [a.b means that the table is there, and [a.b] means that the table holds a setting of its own, not only tables. A part that the record already holds stays. before_remove A command that runs before the packages go, for example pre-commit uninstall.

title: The files of the stack
text: This file names each shared file that a part can go to. A line file, such as .gitignore, needs no entry. Each entry has these keys: Key What it means format lines, toml, json, yaml or hooks. include How the part reaches its own file. extend is the extend key of ruff.toml. extends is the extends list of tsconfig.json and biome.json. pointer is a line in AGENTS.md that names a file. instead Another name of the same file. A part of biome.json goes to biome.jsonc when only that file exists. create false when the installer must not make the file. pyproject.toml comes from uv init only. list and key For YAML: the list that holds the units, and the key that names each item. .pre-commit-config.yaml has repos, named by repo. comments For a line file: html when the comments are HTML comments, as in AGENTS.md.

title: The files of the stack
text: The record has these keys: Key What it holds Example version The version of the format. 2 profiles The installed profiles. ["python"] choices Each role, on or off. {"cx": false, "jagt-protocol": false, "prose": true, "reporter": false, "tasker": true} tools The installed tools. ["python:lint", "python:test"] variants The variant of each role that has variants. {"tasker": "git"} owned_packages The packages that the installer added, keyed by their place in the manifest. A removal takes out only these. For Python the place is profile:group. For TypeScript it is the profile, because npm has no groups. {"python:lint": ["pre-commit", "ruff"]} generated The hash of index.just and of each  .just that the installer wrote. started true when the installer wrote the starter Justfile. true parts Each unit of each shared file. See below. parts_version The version of the format of parts. 1 pending_tools, removing_tools, removing_profiles Work that a run that failed did not finish. The next run finishes it. parts_log_end The id of the last entry of the old log that moved into parts, for a project of an older installer. The installer keeps any other key that it finds in the record. One old key, added_packages, goes. An entry moves into owned_packages when its tool is a tool of a profile that the run turns on, keeps or turns off. The installer drops the other entries. parts is keyed by the shared file, then by the unit. For example: "parts": { ".gitignore": { ".venv": {"state": "added", "needs": ["python"], "holder": "python"} }, "pyproject.toml": { "tool.uv.default-groups": {"state": "added", "needs": ["python"], "holder": "python", "value": "all", "made": ["tool", "tool.uv"]} }, "ruff.toml": { "extend": {"state": "added", "needs": ["python:lint"], "holder": "python:lint", "value": ".agents/config/python/ruff.toml"} }, ".agents/config/python/ruff.toml": { "(own file)": {"state": "added", "holder": "python:lint", "needs": ["python:lint"], "hash": "7ca1..."} } } The name of a unit depends on the format of the file: Format Unit name Example lines The line, without a slash at the end. .venv TOML The dotted key. tool.uv.default-groups TOML include The include key. extend JSON include The include list with its value. extends["./.agents/config/typescript/tsconfig.json"] YAML The list, and the key of the item. repos[repo=https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit] hooks The event, the group, and the command. hooks.PreToolUse {"matcher": "Bash"} $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/raw-git-write-guard.sh An entry has these fields: Field What it means state One of the states below. needs Each owner that needs the unit. holder The owner that holds the unit now. When it goes, the next owner in needs holds it. value The value that the installer wrote, for a unit file. made What the installer made for the unit, for example the tables tool and tool.uv. They go with the last unit inside them. file For a file with two names: the file that holds the unit. A part of biome.json has biome.json or biome.jsonc. hash For an own file or a whole file: the hash of what the installer wrote. earlier Only after a run that stopped: other values that the file can hold for the unit. unsure Only after a run that stopped and a later run that could not read the file. just install --check fails until a run reads the file. The states are these: State Meaning added The installer added the unit. It goes when no owner needs it. present The unit was in the file before its owner came. It is yours, and stays. declined You deleted the unit. The installer does not add it again. kept The whole file is yours, with no part. You changed a whole config file of an older installer, or you made again a file that you had deleted. seeded A starter, such as the first AGENTS.md. It is yours from the start. Some keys of parts are not units. Each one starts with a bracket: Key What it means (own file) The file is an own file of an owner. (whole file) The file is a whole file of a package from before the parts. (file) The whole file is yours. The installer adds no part to it. (starter) A role wrote the file from its starter. (seed) An older installer wrote the file from its seed.

title: The files of the stack
text: A part has one name in the record, the name in profile.json, for example biome.json. The file that holds it can have another name. Biome reads biome.json, else biome.jsonc, and it uses biome.json when both are there. Each entry of the part saves the file that holds it, in file. The installer accepts only biome.json or biome.jsonc there. When only biome.jsonc is there, the part goes to biome.jsonc. When you add a biome.json later, the next run moves the part. It takes the units out of biome.jsonc and adds them to biome.json. A unit that you deleted stays out. just install --check names a part that the next run will move. If one of the two files is a symlink, the installer leaves the part alone. Each run and just install --check say so. The own file that the part includes stays, also after you uninstall its tool. A record of an older installer has no file. The installer then looks for the units in biome.json first, then in biome.jsonc.

title: The files of the stack
section: The layout of a JSON file
text: The installer writes each JSON file that it changes as the Biome formatter writes it. So just lint passes on the file. It reads the Biome config of the project to find the layout: the config in biome.json, else biome.jsonc, with its comments; each local file that its extends names, from the folder of the file that names it. A local file is a name that starts with ./ or ../, or ends with .json or .jsonc. Any other name is a package, and the installer does not read it; each entry of overrides whose includes match the file. It takes these settings, as Biome does: Setting Default lineWidth 80 indentStyle tab indentWidth 2 expand auto lineEnding lf json.formatter.trailingCommas none Each override is a layer after the config, and a later layer wins. In one layer, json.formatter wins over formatter. A project with no Biome config keeps the indent of each file. The installer does not cover these cases: formatter.useEditorconfig. The installer does not read .editorconfig. Set the layout in the Biome config. trailingCommas set to all with no json.parser.allowTrailingCommas. Biome then asks for a comma after the last item of a .json file, and its parser rejects that comma. The installer writes no such comma, so the file stays valid JSON. tsconfig.json, jsconfig.json and .jsonc files take the comma. biome.json never does.

title: The files of the stack
text: The installer writes one record for each package, for example .agents/jnterfaces-install.json. The tasker role uses .agents/gest-git-install.json, the name in the catalog. A profile package gets one too, for example .agents/jnprofile-python-install.json. The main keys are these: Key What it holds schema_version The version of the format. package, source_repository The package and the repository of its clone. source_revision The commit of the clone that the run installed. source_worktree_dirty true when the clone had changes that are not committed. source_requested_commit The commit that the run asked for, if any. skills, skill_folders The installed skills. extras The extra files and folders of install_extras.files. managed_files The hash of each file that the package copied in. A file whose hash is not the recorded hash is yours, and the installer does not overwrite it. claude_links The links in .claude/skills that the installer made. merged_hooks, created_settings, seeds For an installer from before the parts.

title: The files of the stack
text: Before a run writes a shared file, it saves this file: {"files": {"biome.json": {"old": {...}, "new": {...}}}} For each file, old is the record before the run and new is the record that the run is writing. "starter": true marks a file that the run writes from a starter. The key is the name of the record, also when the file is biome.jsonc. When a run stops, the next run reads this file. So it can still take out a part that the stopped run added. A run that works deletes the file. Git ignores it.

title: The files of the stack
text: Each run that changes a file adds one line: {"kind": "history", "id": "2026-10-31T14:04:22Z-47bb", "command": "just install --profile python --defaults", "changes": {"ruff.toml": "units", ".gitignore": "lines", "...": "..."}, "sources": {"jnterfaces": "b4c8b65...", "jnprofile-python": "3a2a1e0..."}} changes gives the kind of change of each file. The kinds are lines, units, whole and own. sources gives the commit of each package. Nothing reads this file to decide what to do. Git ignores it.

title: The files of the stack
text: File Can you edit it? Justfile Yes. It is yours. Put the recipes of the project in it. A shared file, such as .gitignore or ruff.toml Yes. A unit that you change or delete is yours, and the installer keeps your change. .agents/config/... and .agents/instructions/... No. The installer writes them again. Put your settings in the shared file, for example ruff.toml or AGENTS.md. .agents/just/... No. A file that you change is yours, and the installer stops changing it. Put your recipes in the Justfile. .agents/skills/... Only if you want to keep the change. The installer then leaves the file alone and names it. .agents/stack.json Only to resolve a Git conflict. Run just install --check after. .agents/*-install.json, .agents/stack-pending.json, .agents/stack-log.jsonl No.

title: The files of the stack
text: just install --check compares parts in .agents/stack.json with the shared files, and changes nothing. It prints each difference, for example: a unit that is gone, or that you changed; a block that lacks its begin or end comment; a part that the next run will move; a run that stopped. It fails in these cases: a block lacks its begin or end comment; a run stopped, or .agents/stack-pending.json is not a file that the installer wrote; an entry is unsure, because a later run could not read its file. Run just install again to finish a run that stopped. just install --dry-run prints each file that a run would change, and writes nothing.

title: How the stack fits together
text: This guide describes the skill stack on the main branch of jnterfaces. It says where each part lives, what a machine needs, and how an install works. Then it builds a project in layers, from a project with no code to a project with the checks of cheesecracker. Each layer says what works now and what does not. The results come from installs into empty Git repositories on 2026-10-29. On 2026-10-31, a new project of each profile was checked again, with code and tests, up to a passing just verify. The section “Gaps to close” says which gaps a later change closed.

title: How the stack fits together
text: Term Meaning skill A folder with a SKILL.md file. An agent reads it to learn one job. package A Git repository that ships skills, for example nossaifd. role The name of a job, for example prose. A package does the job, so the package can change and the role name stays. profile A language setup, for example python. A profile package, such as jnprofile-python, ships it. tool One unit of the setup of a profile, for example lint. It brings packages, config files and recipes. manifest The file that lists the dependencies of the project: pyproject.toml or package.json. record A JSON file in .agents/ that lists what the installer wrote, with a hash of each file. mixin One layer that you add to a project, for example a role or a tool.

title: How the stack fits together
text: The stack has parts in four places: Place What it holds GitHub, rahuldave/... The source of each package: jnterfaces, agent_gest_git_skills, nossaifd, sklanes, and the profile packages jnprofile-python and jnprofile-typescript. The clone folder One Git clone of each package. The default folder is ~/.local/share/skill-packages. The project Copies of the skills in .agents/skills, the recipes in .agents/just, the records, and .agents/stack.json. The machine The programs: git, just, uv, and the programs that some roles need. The packages and their roles are in this table: Role Package What it installs Default none, always installed jnterfaces the just skill, the installer file .agents/install.just always cx jnterfaces the cx skill no jagt-protocol jnterfaces the jagt-protocol skill no prose nossaifd the nossaifd skill, its guide and check.py yes tasker agent_gest_git_skills the g* skills, the agent hooks, the starter AGENTS.md yes reporter sklanes the lanes skill no Only jnterfaces has an installer, scripts/install_stack.py. The other packages list their files in skill-package.json. The list of packages, roles and profiles is in stack.json of jnterfaces. A profile package also has profile.json, which lists its tools. The clone folder. The installer looks for each package in the folder that SKILL_PACKAGES_DIR names. If the variable is not set, it looks in the folder that holds the jnterfaces clone that runs. If a clone is missing, the installer clones it from GitHub. Each run prints the folder. just install finds the jnterfaces clone from two variables. JNTERFACES_DIR names the clone. Otherwise, the clone is in SKILL_PACKAGES_DIR, by default ~/.local/share/skill-packages. The project does not save the folder, so export the variable in your shell profile, for example export SKILL_PACKAGES_DIR=~/Projects on this machine. If you set none, just install clones new copies into ~/.local/share/skill-packages.

title: How the stack fits together
text: A machine needs git, just and uv. The installer, Python, the Python tools and Node all come through uv. The roles need more programs: Role or tool Program How the stack handles a missing program tasker gest The installer prints a warning and installs the skills. tasker hooks but (GitButler) The hooks check for it, and they work without it. cx cx The skill describes a fallback. jagt-protocol jagt The skill describes a fallback. reporter node 22 or later The package says to run node with uvx --from 'nodejs-wheel==24.*' node.

title: How the stack fits together
text: The installer runs these steps: It reads the roles, profiles and tools from the command line and from .agents/stack.json. If neither names a profile, it looks at the files of the project. For example, pyproject.toml turns on the python profile. It checks each package. If a check fails, it writes nothing. It copies the skills and other files of each role and profile into the project, and it writes one record for each package. It saves the choices in .agents/stack.json. If the project has no Justfile, it writes the starter Justfile. If a tool of a profile is to be added and the project has no manifest, it makes one, with uv init --bare or npm init --yes. It adds the packages of each tool, with uv add --group or npm install --save-dev. After the package commands succeed, it writes the shared files, such as .gitignore, and the config files of the tools. “Shared files and the log” below tells how. It writes the recipes of the installed tools in .agents/just. After each step, it saves the record and writes the recipes again. A later just install with no names installs the same set again, from the clones as they are. To get new commits of the packages, run just install --update. It pulls the jnterfaces clone and the clone of each package that the run installs. It skips a clone with no upstream branch, and it prints “Not updated”. The installer writes a config file of a tool, for example ruff.toml, when the project has none. It takes the file out with its tool only when nobody changed it. An edited file stays as you left it. The installer does not overwrite a file of a package that you edited. It names the file, and it installs the other files. The record keeps the hash of the install, so the next run and a removal still see the edit. To get the new version, undo the edit, or remove the file, and run just install again. A file that no install wrote, in the place of a file of a package, still stops the install, and the installer writes nothing. The first install. A new project has no Justfile, so it has no just install. Run the installer from the clone for the first install: uv run ~/Projects/jnterfaces/scripts/install_stack.py --target . prose A named role asks no questions, so the command turns on prose only. With a named profile or tool and no named role, a terminal asks about each role. After that, the project has .agents/install.just. A Justfile that has the line import? '.agents/install.just' gets the recipes just install and just uninstall. The agents. Codex reads skills from .agents/skills. Claude Code reads skills from .claude/skills. So for each installed skill, the installer makes the link .claude/skills/NAME, which points to ../../.agents/skills/NAME. When the skill goes, the link goes. The installer leaves alone any other file or link in .claude/skills, and a .claude or .claude/skills that is a link or a file. A link that you remove. If you remove a link, no later install makes it again. If you remove the whole .claude/skills folder, the next install makes all the links again. copier. .agents/install.just defines the variable jn_copier, which runs copier 9 through uvx. copier makes files from a template, and copier update brings in a later version of the template and keeps your edits. So a recipe can use {{jn_copier}} copy TEMPLATE FOLDER with no install.

title: How the stack fits together
text: Each tool of a profile has one recipe file, for example .agents/just/python/lint.just. The profile package installs these files. just install then writes two kinds of file in .agents/just: python.just, a module for each profile. It imports the recipe files of the installed tools only, and its verify runs their checks. Its recipes run in the folder of the project. just python lint runs one. index.just, which .agents/install.just imports. It has a mod line for each profile. In a project that jnterfaces started, it also has a combined recipe for each recipe name. So just lint runs the lint of each language. Its verify runs the verify of each language, then git diff --check. A project that jnterfaces started. When the project has no Justfile, the installer writes the starter Justfile, and .agents/stack.json records "started": true. The starter Justfile has set allow-duplicate-recipes. So a recipe in the Justfile itself with the name of a recipe of the index, such as lint, takes its place. It does not take the place of the recipe of a language, so just python verify still runs the lint of the profile. A recipe of yours can also depend on a recipe of the index, for example ci: verify. A project that jnterfaces did not start, such as one with its own Justfile, gets the modules only, for example just python lint. A name that meets a name of the index. An alias, a module, or a recipe in a project without set allow-duplicate-recipes can have the name of a recipe or a module of the index. Then the Justfile does not parse. The installer checks the Justfile after it writes the index. If it does not parse, the installer writes the index with the modules only, then with none, and it names the clash. So just install keeps working. Rename the name of the project to get the recipes back. The record. .agents/stack.json holds the hash of each file that just install wrote in .agents/just, under generated. The installer changes or removes a file only while its hash is the recorded one. It keeps any other file, and it names that file. Put your own recipes in the Justfile. With more than one language, a combined recipe gives the same arguments to each language. To give arguments to one language, run just python test x.

title: How the stack fits together
text: Each layer adds one mixin. Start at layer 0, and add the layers that the project needs. Each command after layer 1 is a recipe of the project. For the shortest path to a full project, with each tool and recipe, read Start a Python or TypeScript project.

title: How the stack fits together
text: mkdir notes && cd notes && git init The project has no code, no manifest and no Justfile.

title: How the stack fits together
text: uv run ~/Projects/jnterfaces/scripts/install_stack.py --target . prose What you get: .agents/skills/just and .agents/skills/nossaifd, with check.py, and their links in .claude/skills. .agents/install.just, the records, and .agents/stack.json. The starter Justfile, which imports .agents/install.just. So just install, just uninstall and just install --help work. Run the checker on the Markdown files that git tracks, or on the pages that you name. Alone, it leaves out AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, which are instructions for agents: just prose just prose -v README.md An agent finds the nossaifd skill by its description, through the link in .claude/skills or the copy in .agents/skills. So it needs no line in an AGENTS.md. What does not work: A project with a manifest gets a profile. If the project has pyproject.toml or package.json on the first install, the installer finds the profile and adds its default tools. To install the role alone, pass --profile '' on the first install. The record then keeps no profile.

title: How the stack fits together
text: just install tasker What you get: The g* skills, which track work with Gest. The agent hooks in .claude/hooks and .codex/hooks, with their entries in .claude/settings.json and .codex/hooks.json. A starter AGENTS.md, if the project has none. The starter is yours from then on. just uninstall tasker takes out only the lines of the role, and the rest of the file stays. Variants. just install tasker=gitwt works on each task in its own Git worktree, and keeps the main checkout on main. The default, tasker=git, works on a branch in the main checkout. The record saves the variant, and just tasker-mode prints it. The jj variant is not ready yet. The worktree recipes. In a project that jnterfaces started, the role adds these recipes: Recipe What it does just worktree-new NAME [BASE] Makes branch NAME in ../ .worktrees/NAME, sets it up, and runs just setup there just worktree-sync Sets up a worktree that another tool made, such as Claude Code just worktrees Lists the worktrees: clean or dirty, merged or not, and the ignored files that a removal deletes just worktrees-prune Removes the clean, merged worktrees that were idle for 2 hours, with no --force. A worktree with outputs or other ignored files that setup did not put there stays A worktree has only the files that Git tracks. So setup follows two files in the main checkout. .worktreeinclude has gitignore patterns, and each ignored file that matches is copied, for example .env. .worktreelink has one path on each line, and each path becomes a symbolic link to the main checkout, for example a large data folder. Claude Code and Conductor read .worktreeinclude; PostHog uses .worktreelink. Commands in a worktree also make ignored files, such as .venv and test caches. just worktrees-prune keeps a worktree with ignored files, so that it never deletes an output. A third file, .worktreedisposable, has gitignore patterns for the ignored files that a command can make again. Those files do not keep a worktree. Each profile adds its lines to this file, in a block of its own. The Python profile names .venv/ and the caches, and the TypeScript profile names node_modules/. What works. The install, the variant and the worktree recipes. The GitButler text of the hooks appears only when but is installed and GitButler owns the checkout. The session-start hook reports worktrees that are ready to prune, and removes nothing. In gitwt, a git commit in the main checkout gets a warning. What does not work: The worktree recipes are missing in a project that jnterfaces did not start. There the skills run the script of the gtw skill directly. The skills need gest. gest does not come through uv. The installer prints a warning when it is missing. The starter AGENTS.md has   fields. You fill them in.

title: How the stack fits together
text: just install --profile python Use --profile typescript for TypeScript. Name a profile once. The installer saves it. What you get with python: The package jnprofile-python, with its recipe files and its skill python-profile. pyproject.toml from uv init --bare, with default-groups = "all", so that uv run has the tools. Its lines in .gitignore and .worktreedisposable, in a block of their own at the start of each file. The default tools lint and test, which the next layers describe, and the recipe just setup. What you get with typescript: The package jnprofile-typescript. uv runs npm and node from the nodejs-wheel package. package.json from npm init --yes, and its lines in .gitignore and .worktreedisposable. The default tools lint and typecheck. A profile also turns on its default roles, tasker and prose, but only in a project with no saved roles.

title: How the stack fits together
text: just install lint Python TypeScript Packages ruff, pre-commit, in the group lint @biomejs/biome@2 Config files ruff.toml, .pre-commit-config.yaml biome.json Recipes just fmt, just lint, just hook just fmt, just lint In just verify fmt --check, lint lint ruff.toml and biome.json leave out .agents, .claude and .codex, because these folders hold copies from other packages. What does not work. The TypeScript profile has no just hook.

title: How the stack fits together
text: just install test Python. The tool adds pytest and pytest-cov to the group test. just test and just cov run pytest. With no arguments, a project with no tests yet passes. A selection that runs no test fails. TypeScript. The tool adds TypeScript and the Node types. just test compiles src into dist, and it runs the tests with node --test. With no .ts file in src yet, it passes.

title: How the stack fits together
text: just install typecheck Python. The tool adds ty to the group lint, and a ty.toml that leaves out .agents, .claude and .codex. just typecheck runs ty check. TypeScript. The tool adds TypeScript and tsconfig.json. just typecheck runs tsc --noEmit. With no .ts file in src yet, it passes.

title: How the stack fits together
section: Layer 7: one check before a commit
text: just verify runs the checks of each installed tool of each language, then git diff --check, which finds whitespace errors. On a new project with the default tools, just verify passes, for Python and for TypeScript. cheesecracker calls this recipe just check. The command contract of the just skill names it verify, and it lets a project map the name.

title: How the stack fits together
section: Layers that the stack does not have yet
text: cheesecracker has these parts, and no profile or tool adds them: Part In cheesecracker A locked setup just setup runs uv sync --locked. The profile runs uv sync. A server just serve and just stop start and stop uvicorn in the background. System tests just test-system runs tests against the running server. Docker just docker-build, just docker-serve, just docker-stop, just docker-shell and just docker-test, with a .dockerignore. Async tests The group test has pytest-asyncio and httpx2. Coverage of one package just cov names the package, --cov=api. Test paths pyproject.toml sets testpaths and pythonpath for pytest. The test tool now sets pythonpath, but not testpaths. CI The class repository cheese-app-ci-cd has a GitHub Actions workflow. No profile writes one.

title: How the stack fits together
text: Adding a mixin. just install NAME adds a role, a tool or a profile, and it saves the choice. A tool that fails runs again at the next install. Removing a mixin. just uninstall NAME takes out a role, a tool or a profile: A role loses its files. Each file that you edited stays. A tool loses the packages that just install added, and its recipes. Each package that the project had before stays. A dependency group that is left empty goes too. A config file of the tool goes when nobody changed it. The lines of the tool go from the shared files, unless another owner needs them. A profile loses each of its tools, its recipe files and its package. The project keeps pyproject.toml or package.json. If a step fails, the next just install goes on with the removal, unless you name the profile again. --profile with a list that leaves out a saved profile also turns that profile off.

title: How the stack fits together
text: Several owners can add a part to one file. An owner is jnterfaces, a profile such as python, a tool of a profile such as python:lint, or a role such as tasker. Each owner adds its part and takes out only its part. notes/plan-shared-files.md and notes/plan-snippets.md give each decision and its reason. scripts/formats.json lists the shared files that a package can add a part to, with the format of each file. The files of the stack gives each key of the record and of the files that the packages ship. Three kinds of part. The format of the file sets the kind: Kind Files What the owner adds A block of lines .gitignore, .worktreedisposable Its lines, in a block of its own at the start of the file An include ruff.toml, tsconfig.json, biome.json, AGENTS.md One line or key that reads an own file, which the installer writes under .agents/config/ or .agents/instructions/ Units ty.toml, pyproject.toml, .pre-commit-config.yaml, .claude/settings.json, .codex/hooks.json Keys, items of a list, or hooks An own file is a file that only the installer writes. Do not edit it. To change a setting, set it in the shared file. Your settings win over the settings of the own file. For example, line-length = 99 in your ruff.toml wins over the line-length = 120 of .agents/config/python/ruff.toml. A block of lines looks like this: # begin lines of python:lint, the lint tool of the python profile, from jnprofile-python at c299beb. # Last written to .gitignore by `just install lint`. The record is parts.".gitignore" in .agents/stack.json. .ruff_cache/ # end lines of python:lint. `just uninstall lint` removes them. Your own lines come after the blocks. In a git ignore file, a later line wins, so a line of yours always wins over a line of a block. In AGENTS.md the comments of a block are HTML comments. A TOML key or a YAML item of a part has one comment on the line before it, which names its owner. The record. The key parts in .agents/stack.json records each unit that the installer added. For each unit, it records the state, the owner that holds the unit, and each owner that needs it. The files are the output of the record. A removal reads the record, never the files, to know what to take out. The states are: State Meaning added The installer added the unit. It goes when no owner needs it. present The unit was in the file before its owner came. It is yours, and stays. declined You deleted the unit. The installer does not add it again. kept You changed a whole config file of an older installer. It stays yours, with no part. seeded A starter, such as the first AGENTS.md. It is yours from the start. How a part goes. A unit that two owners need stays while either owner is on. When the owner that holds it goes, it passes to the other owner. A unit that you delete stays out. A shared file that you delete stays deleted in the same way, and its own file goes. A unit that you change is yours. It stays when its owners go, and the output names it. Two owners that need one unit with two values stop the run, which names both owners. ruff.toml takes one extend, so it has one owner. A line that you add inside a block moves after the blocks at the next run. When the last part goes and nothing else is left in the file, the file goes. Files that the installer leaves alone. A tsconfig.json or a biome.jsonc with comments is not plain JSON. The installer does not change it, and the output prints the include to add by hand. An extend of your own in ruff.toml stays, and the installer writes no own file. If git ignores an own file, the run stops, because a fresh clone needs the own file. A guard. The lint tool of the python profile adds no part to ruff.toml when pyproject.toml has a [tool.ruff] table. An extend there would change your settings and the format of the whole code base. The guard stops a new part only. A part that is there stays when you add [tool.ruff] later. Roles. A role adds its parts in the same way. The tasker role adds a starter AGENTS.md once. If you delete it while the role is installed, it stays deleted. The role also adds a line to AGENTS.md that points to .agents/instructions/tasker.md. Its hooks are units of .claude/settings.json and .codex/hooks.json. The SessionStart hook of the role prints the rules file, so both Claude and Codex read the rules. Claude Code and Codex show a long hook output only as a preview and a file. So the first line of the output asks the agent to read the whole file. The log is a history. .agents/stack-log.jsonl gets one entry for each run that changes a file. Nothing reads it to decide what to do. The jnterfaces block of .gitignore names it, so git does not keep it. A run that stops. Before a run writes a file, it saves .agents/stack-pending.json with the old and new record of each file. The next run reads it, so it can still take out a part that the stopped run added. git does not keep this file either. Branches. When two branches change .agents/stack.json, git gives a conflict in it. Resolve it as for any file. A merge can keep the blocks of both sides and the record of one side. Then the next run takes each block of a known owner into the record. Check and dry run. just install --check compares the record with the files, prints each difference, and changes nothing. It fails for a block that lacks its begin or end comment, and for a run that stopped. Run just install again to finish such a run. --dry-run prints each file that a run would change. Projects of an older installer. The first run of this installer moves the record from the old log to parts, once: The lines of the old log become units of the record. A config file that the old installer wrote and that nobody changed becomes an own file and an include. A config file that you changed stays yours, with no include. To have the include, delete the file and run just install again. An AGENTS.md that the old installer wrote and that nobody changed becomes the starter and a pointer. One that you changed stays yours. The hook still prints the rules. The hooks that a role merged become units of the role. The output asks you to run git rm --cached .agents/stack-log.jsonl once. If an older installer on another branch adds an entry to the log after the move, the run stops. Run the new installer on that branch first. Each person on a project moves to the new installer at the same time. Removing lint takes out the Git hook. Before just uninstall lint removes pre-commit, it runs uv run --group lint pre-commit uninstall. It runs only when the pre-commit Git hook runs the Python of the project. If the command fails, the removal stops, and the next just install tries it again.

title: How the stack fits together
text: The profile packages closed the gaps of the recipes. The recipes follow the tools, a project with no code has a Justfile, and verify runs only the checks that are installed. These gaps are open: Add a profile for a web service, for example jnprofile-fastapi, with the tools serve, docker and system-test. These parts are not for each Python project, so they are a profile of their own and not tools of the python profile. A project names both, with just install --profile python,fastapi. Two profiles with the same manifest, pyproject.toml, are not tested yet. Save the clone folder in the project. The installer fixes closed these gaps: .claude/skills links for each installed skill. An edited file no longer stops an install. A named role asks no questions. The installer script reads SKILL_PACKAGES_DIR, and each run prints the folder. Removing lint takes out the Git hook. The role recipes closed these gaps: just prose checks the Markdown of the project. just uninstall tasker takes the lines of the role out of AGENTS.md. jnprofile-typescript is on GitHub.
